question.prompt: A polynomial \[ \begin{aligned} &P(x) = c_{2004} x^{2004} + c_{2003} x^{2003} \\ &\quad {}+ \cdots + c_1 x + c_0 \end{aligned} \] has real coefficients with \(c_{2004} \ne 0\) and \(2004\) distinct complex zeros \(z_k = a_k + b_k i,\) \(1 \le k \le 2004\) with \(a_k\) and \(b_k\) real, \(a_1 = b_1 = 0,\) and \[\sum_{k=1}^{2004} a_k = \sum_{k=1}^{2004} b_k.\] Which of the following quantities can be a nonzero number?

solutions.explanation:
Real coefficients impose a useful symmetry: if \(z\) is a zero, then its conjugate \(\overline z\) is also a zero, because
\[
P(\overline z)=\overline{P(z)}=0.
\]
Every nonreal zero therefore pairs with a zero having the opposite imaginary part. Real zeros have imaginary part zero, so
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{2004}b_k=0.
\]
The given equality now implies \(\sum a_k=0\), making choice \(\text{D}\) zero as well.

To connect this with the coefficients, factor the polynomial using all its zeros:
\[
P(x)=c_{2004}\prod_{k=1}^{2004}(x-z_k).
\]
A term of degree \(2003\) is obtained by selecting \(-z_k\) from one factor and \(x\) from every other factor. Consequently
\[
c_{2003}=-c_{2004}\sum_{k=1}^{2004}z_k=0,
\]
since both the real and imaginary parts of the root sum are zero. This eliminates \(\text{B}\). Also, \(z_1=0\), so \(c_0=P(0)=0\), eliminating \(\text{A}\).

Among the remaining \(2003\) zeros, all nonreal zeros occur in pairs. Since \(2003\) is odd, at least one remaining zero must be real. Its imaginary part is zero, so
\[
b_2b_3\cdots b_{2004}=0.
\]
Thus \(\text{C}\) is always zero.

We still need an example showing that \(\text{E}\) can be nonzero. Take
\[
Q(x)=x(x+1)(x+2)(x-3)
\prod_{j=4}^{1003}(x^2-j^2).
\]
This is a monic polynomial of degree \(4+2(1000)=2004\). Its zeros are the distinct real numbers \(0,-1,-2,3\) and \(\pm j\) for \(4\le j\le1003\). Their sum is zero: the first four sum to zero, and each remaining pair cancels. All imaginary parts are zero, so every required condition holds.

None of these zeros is \(1\), so \(Q(1)\ne0\). Evaluating at \(1\) adds all coefficients, and the constant coefficient is \(Q(0)=0\). Therefore its positive-power coefficient sum is \(Q(1)-Q(0)=Q(1)\ne0\). The quantity that can be nonzero is \(\boxed{\sum_{k=1}^{2004}c_k}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
